answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 416 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the opal seed, the ledge timing is verifiable from the pigment record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 168 keys therefore pays 168 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
